column1: Training & Inference|A deployed support model is drafting a reply to a new ticket. Which stage is this?|Inference using a trained model|Retraining the model on these tickets|Treating reply generation as fixed-rule matching|Training learns patterns; inference processes new inputs.

Generative AI|A team needs a first draft from interview notes. Which capability should it evaluate?|Generative AI summarization and drafting|Predicting next week's sales with a forecasting model|Replacing summarization with fixed-field validation|Generated content still needs evaluation for factuality, usefulness and review effort.

Predictive ML|A store estimates next week's demand from historical sales. What is the core capability?|Predicting outcomes from historical patterns|Only rewriting historical sales reports with a generative model|Only comparing the readability of generated text|Evaluate prediction errors and their inventory and business impacts.

Unstructured Data|What type of data includes customer recordings, email bodies and images?|Unstructured data|Transaction records normalized into fixed fields|Numerical reports with explicitly defined columns|Data format affects extraction, quality evaluation and usability.

Data Quality|Training data contains duplicates and missing values, and performance is poor. What should the team do?|Investigate and improve the relevant data quality|Only increase model size while keeping the same data|Increase data volume before checking duplicates and missing values|Data issues affect AI results and cannot be solved by changing the interface alone.

AI Management System|How should an organization interpret ISO/IEC 42001 when defining AI responsibilities and processes?|An organizational AI management system standard|An evaluation standard that guarantees model accuracy|A technical specification limited to prompt formats|Awareness of a standard is different from a guarantee of model performance.

Rules vs AI|An expense policy requires approval above a fixed amount. What is an appropriate first approach?|Deterministic rules implementing explicit conditions|Letting a general-purpose model freely decide each approval|Replacing the rules before evaluating benefits|Technology should fit the problem; a fixed rule does not need to become AI.

Agent Authority|An agent can issue refunds. How should large-refund risk be constrained?|Limit authorized actions and require approval and logging|Grant broad permissions and rely on retrospective spot checks|Only tell the agent to be cautious in its prompt|Action capabilities need permission boundaries, oversight and intervention mechanisms.

Monitoring|The user population changes after deployment and prediction performance falls. What is appropriate?|Monitor changes, investigate causes and correct them|Evaluate only once at deployment acceptance|Replace the model without investigating the change|AI needs ongoing performance monitoring; deployment does not end maintenance.

Shadow AI|Employees do not know which tools are allowed. How can unapproved use be reduced?|Publish approved, restricted and evaluated tools with guidance|Only publish a list of prohibited tools|Tell employees to judge data sensitivity entirely on their own|Clear tool policies need training and usable compliant workflows.

Prompt Design|The model produces unsuitable long responses despite sufficient material. What should be improved first?|Clarify the task, context and output format|Add more unrelated examples to the request|Only change the model without clarifying requirements|Better instructions express the task more clearly, but output quality still needs evaluation.

Context Window|Important information is lost when a very long document is added to a request. What matters?|Token and context limits and material selection|Increase output length without selecting relevant material|Use fine-tuning alone to fix an overlong request|Select relevant content and organize context rather than assuming unlimited capacity.

RAG|Support answers must reflect frequently updated company policies. What should be considered?|Retrieve relevant, authorized and current policies|Fine-tune every policy change before considering an update process|Only optimize response format while retaining the old sources|Retrieval supplements information, but quality, currency and permissions still need management.

Fine-tuning|A team wants further training to improve task behavior. What should it evaluate?|Suitable training examples, maintenance cost and evaluation|Add retrieval before assessing the behavioral gap|Only lengthen prompts and ignore training-example quality|Fine-tuning adjusts behavior through training; suitability depends on the actual capability gap.

Business Objective|A team wants to buy the strongest model before finding a use. What should it clarify first?|The business problem and desired outcome|Choose the model first and reshape goals around it|Set one purchasing budget before discussing goals|AI capability must connect to business outcomes; a technology name is not a requirement.

Build Buy Partner|A project lacks talent and has a tight deadline. How should delivery be chosen?|Compare budget, time, capabilities and supplier options|Compare suppliers only by first-year purchase price|Decide whether to build only by customizability|Build, buy and partner choices depend on actual conditions.

Prioritization|Two proposals compete for resources. How should they be ranked?|Compare value, feasibility and strategic fit|Choose the project with the strongest demo|Compare projected returns without implementation constraints|Investment decisions need both benefits and delivery conditions, including the option to pause.

AI Unsuitability|A reliable simple rule solves the problem. What is a sound decision approach?|Compare the rule-based alternative with AI|Assume AI takes priority and optimize costs later|Compare model vendors without considering a rule-based solution|Evaluation should include feasible alternatives that do not use AI.

Continuity|A critical workflow is moving to a new AI platform. What should be retained?|Performance validation, cutover planning and fallback|Complete the switch before planning fallback|Compare purchase prices only, ignoring operational changes|Migration must consider data, cost, performance and business continuity.

Baseline|What should be recorded before a pilot to assess improvement?|Actual time and quality of the existing process|Only record average time after launch|Only use a supplier's industry-average efficiency figures|Without a comparable starting point, attributing improvement is difficult.

KPI|Support drafts are faster but contain more errors. How should the result be evaluated?|Observe efficiency, quality and review cost together|Use generation speed as the main acceptance criterion|Only measure satisfaction, ignoring errors and cost|Business value depends on useful outcomes and their costs.

Released Capacity|Ten hours are freed each week but payroll is unchanged. How should this be described?|Time released for other work|Cash savings calculated directly from wage rates|Count both staff reductions and extra output without conditions|More available time and lower cash expenditure require separate evidence.

Leading Indicator|Training completion rises early in a rollout. How should it be interpreted?|An early signal that still needs outcome tracking|Treat training completion as realized financial benefit|Stop tracking outcomes once early indicators improve|Early signals are different from realized business outcomes.

Total Cost|What should be included when comparing AI returns?|Deployment, usage, training, review and maintenance costs|Only model-call fees and purchase expenditure|Deployment costs but not training and review|Return estimates need a clear and complete cost boundary.

Double Counting|The same time saving is counted as both payroll savings and extra output. What is needed first?|Evidence that the benefits are independent and realizable|Convert both benefits to money and add them|Choose the larger amount without defining benefit boundaries|The same benefit cannot be counted twice without justification.

Competitive Landscape|Competitors begin adopting AI. What should the company examine first?|Actual effects on customers, operations and competitive position|Use competitors' spending as its own budget|Buy the same tools before comparing customer value|Competitive analysis must reflect the company's goals and real strengths.

Business Model|AI changes how a service is delivered. What should be evaluated?|Changes in customer value, delivery and revenue logic|Reposition the service merely by adding AI labels|Compare generation speed without delivery or revenue analysis|Turning capability into value needs a concrete business explanation.

Durable Advantage|Several firms can buy the same model. What supports differentiation?|Sustainable advantages in data, workflows and organizational capability|Treat purchasing the same foundation model as an exclusive barrier|Compare one benchmark score without operational capability|Advantage should come from sustainable business capability and operational improvement.

Investment Level|Industries have different AI maturity levels. How should investment be set?|Combine competitive dynamics, maturity and internal conditions|Match a competitor's disclosed budget exactly|Base all investment solely on the lowest short-term cost|Investment must fit the environment and implementation capability.

Fairness|Overall accuracy is good but some groups perform much worse. What is appropriate?|Examine relevant subgroup performance and improve it|Raise overall accuracy before looking at group differences|Only increase sample size without distinguishing groups|An overall average does not replace evaluation of relevant group differences.

Explainability|Business users need to understand an AI judgment. What matters?|Explanations and evidence appropriate to the users|Only show overall accuracy|Provide more technical terms without explaining the judgment|Explanations should support judgment, not replace verification.

Privacy|A proposal uses sensitive customer data. What should be checked first?|Purpose, authorization and data-protection requirements|Collect all customer data before deciding its purpose|Only add confidentiality instructions without checking authorization|Data use requires authorization and implemented protections.

Governance by Design|When should responsibility and risk controls enter an AI project?|During planning and throughout operation|Wait until the pilot ends before defining governance|Prioritize speed and defer controls until production launch|Responsible AI belongs in planning and operations, not just final documentation.

Human Oversight|What makes human review of high-risk outputs effective?|Information, time, authority and escalation channels|Keep a confirmation button without allocating review time|Show reviewers a conclusion without necessary evidence|Oversight needs practical intervention capability rather than ceremonial sign-off.

Accountability|What matters when forming an AI governance team?|Cross-functional collaboration with clear responsibilities|Assign only technical staff and postpone business ownership|Delegate all company use decisions to the supplier|Cross-functional participation still requires explicit accountability.

Compliance Risk|How should compliance be assessed when a workflow adopts AI?|Identify requirements relevant to its workflow and data use|Reuse a generic IT checklist without analyzing the use case|Deploy first and discover requirements from incidents|Applicable requirements depend on the specific business context and intended use.

Access Control|An employee asks about a file they cannot access. How should disclosure be prevented?|Enforce permissions at data and tool layers|Ask the model to decide authorization in a prompt|Only provide confidentiality training without changing permissions|Confidentiality instructions cannot replace implemented access controls.

Lifecycle Risk|AI applications have different risks. How should governance be allocated?|Classify risks and adjust controls across the lifecycle|Assign a uniform level based on model size|Classify only at project approval and never update it|Governance priorities should track real risks and changes in use.

Production Controls|What is needed when AI moves from pilot to production?|Monitoring, owners, incident handling and fallback|Keep the demo environment and only add users|Only verify model performance without operating ownership|Ongoing operation needs operational and governance conditions.

Bias Drift|Fairness was assessed before deployment. What is needed afterward?|Continue monitoring as data and use conditions change|End group evaluation after one pre-launch check|Monitor overall accuracy without reassessing group differences|Bias can arise at multiple stages and change with operating conditions.

Content & IP|What should a content-generation deployment consider?|Harmful content and intellectual-property risks|Only deploy a content filter without checking rights and uses|Only check input sources without assessing output harms|Controls must cover content uses and relevant rights.

Hallucination|A fluent answer lacks reliable support. What is appropriate?|Verify evidence, use appropriate retrieval, evaluate and review|Improve fluency to make it appear more credible|Only add retrieval without verifying relevance or support|Retrieval and review need quality controls; no single measure guarantees zero errors.

Readiness|What should be assessed before buying a model to establish implementation readiness?|Leadership, people, data, process and governance capabilities|Use purchasing budget as the main readiness measure|Treat enthusiastic volunteers as representative of all employees|Readiness includes implementation conditions beyond the model.

Maturity|A department has many experiments but no stable production capability. How should it be assessed?|Distinguish experimentation from enterprise-scale operations|Judge maturity by the number of experiments|Use self-assessment only without production evidence|Maturity should reflect sustainable operating capability.

Capability Gap|A pilot cannot scale. What should be identified first?|Specific gaps in people, processes, technology and governance|Increase the tool-purchasing budget first|Mandate use before investigating process barriers|Investment should address the actual obstacles.

Capability Investment|Many gaps exist but resources are limited. How should work be ordered?|Prioritize against strategy and current maturity|Invest first in the easiest capability to demonstrate|Split budget equally according to the number of gaps|Readiness development needs clear priorities and an executable path.

Data Readiness|Departmental data is inconsistent and hard to access. What should be assessed first?|Quality, accessibility and the impact of data silos|Increase compute without analyzing silos|Select a model before establishing data availability|A usable data foundation determines practical feasibility.

Data Ownership|Shared information is rarely updated. What should be clarified?|Data owners, sharing rules and maintenance processes|Assign users without maintenance responsibility|Expand sharing without update or authorization rules|Ownership and sharing rules support sustained usability.

Infrastructure|How should infrastructure for an AI workload be selected?|Assess real needs, scalability and operational support|Size every environment for the minimum pilot load|Buy the largest configuration before defining requirements|Infrastructure must support expected workloads and operational needs.

Sponsorship|Cross-departmental adoption is blocked. How should support be built?|Establish executive backing and empower business champions|Train frontline staff and leave resource coordination to them|Publish sponsorship slogans without empowering champions|Support must enable coordination and removal of obstacles.

Communication|Employees worry about changing roles. What is an appropriate response?|Explain timing, expectations and role impacts and address concerns|Only describe benefits and avoid role changes|Only announce launch timing without addressing work impacts|Transparent communication helps employees understand real changes.

Resistance|Employees avoid AI because mistakes may be punished. What intervention fits?|Understand concerns and create a safe learning and feedback environment|Add adoption targets without examining concerns|Change tools without addressing experimentation and feedback|Cultural issues need leadership action and learning support.

Workforce Development|Roles have different tasks. How should training be designed?|Fit role-specific tasks and include responsible use|Give one tool introduction and assess attendance only|Teach operation without boundaries or verification|Development should enable appropriate use in real work.

Human AI Collaboration|AI assists repetitive tasks. How can human roles evolve?|More judgment, oversight, empathetic communication and creativity|Only speed up manual handling without changing oversight|Let AI take over all judgment with retrospective spot checks|Role design should combine human strengths with AI capabilities.

Iterative Scaling|Pilot metrics are promising. How should rollout scope be decided?|Validate transfer conditions and iterate in stages|Copy the volunteer pilot to every team immediately|Expand first and establish monitoring and support later|Larger scale can expose data, cost, user and support differences.

Center of Excellence|Several teams repeatedly solve the same problems. What could help?|A CoE sharing capabilities, standards and collaboration|Centralize all business judgments in one approval team|Keep departments separate without reusing capabilities|Collaboration should enable reuse while retaining business accountability.

Feedback|How should long-term value be tracked after rollout?|Collect ongoing feedback and observe success measures|Only track early-launch satisfaction|Keep success stories and postpone negative feedback|Operational feedback supports timely correction and continued improvement.

Production Transition|How should a project move from experiment to business operation?|Define governance, operations, responsibilities and support|Expand users before arranging operational handover|Only hand over model files without governance and support|Important workflows need stable operations and continuity arrangements.
